terms.gloss: up to now, as yet, still
evidence: Cic. Att. 7.2: ūnam adhūc ā tē epistulam accēperam (Lewis & Short)
Ter. Ph. 4.3.20: cēlābitur itidem ut cēlāta adhūc est (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Strictly “up to this point”: what has been so until now. With a negative it is “not yet” (adhūc nōn, or nōndum). In a question like “are you still awake?” Latin uses etiam: Etiam vigilās?.

phrases.latin: itaque nēmō adhūc convenīre mē voluit, cui fuerim occupātus
phrases.english: and so no one who has wanted to see me has yet found me tied up
Are you awake yet? — I am

sources: Lewis & Short: adhuc · Lewis & Short: etiam
